utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. Good morning, Mr. Suljevic. I thank you again for coming to the Tribunal from such a long distance, despite your busy schedule. I appreciate it very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I take it you have three hours more to conclude your cross-examination, but I believe you can do that by the end of the second session today. Let's begin -- let's continue your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Good morning to all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Suljevic.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning to all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is Sarajevo where it used to be?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sarajevo is always where it used to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That is part of a folk song of ours. That's why I'm putting it in those words, Is Sarajevo where it used to be? So, Mr. Suljevic, you had occasion to see an order of General Milosevic related to operations against Hrasnica, and in one statement, you said that you were astonished by it, or words to that effect. Tell me, why was it that you were astonished? And, please, could you keep it as brief as possible?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, the order was to select a target, a civilian target, in such a way so as to cause the largest number of casualties once the projectile is activated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, the problem is in one single word. It doesn't say "civilian target" anywhere, it says "select a target." Are you trying to say that in Hrasnica there weren't any legitimate targets anywhere?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what was a legitimate target for you in Hrasnica, and I don't know where the lines were, I don't know where the military commands were, and so on and so forth. But just like Hrasnica, Sarajevo was a target throughout the war. That is to say, all of us who were there were casualties throughout the time. We were the victims of these attacks coming from the hills.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Excellent. Let us shed more light on this, one thing at a time. Can we have 1D -- actually, I think it's 65 ter 10693. That's the Serbian version, 10693. So could you please read this? It's not too long. Could you please read the first paragraph in its entirety? We have it in English and in Serbian. Could we please have both versions here for the interpreters. Can you please have a look at this first paragraph: "It's already been three days ..."

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "It's already been three days that the Muslim forces have been attacking the positions of the --"

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "... Sarajevo Light Infantry Brigade."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "And the attacks are particularly pronounced in the sector of the Famos factory. Several of ours soldiers and a large number of civilians have been wounded."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The next paragraph, please.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "In order to thwart the enemy and give them a warning so they are forced to accept the truce, I hereby order: "The Ilidza Brigade will immediately prepare a launcher with an aerial bomb and transport the bomb for launching. "The most profitable target must be selected in Hrasnica or Sokolovic colony, where the greatest casualties and material damage would be inflicted. "Inform me personally of the readiness for implementation of this task."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Suljevic. Let us please focus on the first paragraph: "As for General Milosevic and his unit in Famos factory," that was held by the Serbs. Are the civilians from Hrasnica a threat to them or the Muslim forces, as is written here?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just know that one of these air-bombs fell near my brother's house. My brother lives in Sokolovic Kolonija, and there weren't any targets there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Suljevic, we'll get to that. First of all, let us deal with this order. Can we see here that as for General Milosevic's forces and positions, who is the threat, civilians or the Muslim forces? And it's during a cease-fire, at that; right? That is clearly stated here. Isn't that right? Don't the first two paragraphs show that the Muslim forces were threatening the lines in positions of the Army of Republika Srpska, for which General Milosevic is responsible, during the cease-fire, and it was from Hrasnica towards the Famos factory the most; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here: "To thwart the enemy and give them a warning so that they are forced to accept this truce, I hereby," and so on and so forth, as I read it out previously.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Let us now go to the one-and-only paragraph of the order, itself. Does it say "civilians" at any point, or "civilian targets"?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't say "military targets" either, as far as I can see. It says: "In Hrasnica or Sokolovic Kolonija, select the most profitable target." We can only guess what the most profitable target may be, but it's the civilian areas that were hit by the air-bomb.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were you in the army, Mr. Suljevic?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did my service in the former JNA in 1983.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you get a rank?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Private first class, but that's not much, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "Profitable target," what does that mean to any military person? Why would "profitable target" mean civilians when it's the army that is carrying out the attack?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said a moment ago that all of Sarajevo was a target throughout the war, and all of Sarajevo was shelled intensively. If this were somewhere at the front-line where there were no civilians, perhaps I might have thought differently. But in town, where we were all casualties and victims, at home, at the market, at work -- as we went to the market, or to work, and back home. A house was hit with a projectile where I lived. A tram was hit --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Suljevic, let us leave that aside now. But this is what these proceedings are all about, whether Sarajevo was a helpless victim of a Serb Army or was it a camp full of legitimate targets. Now I'm asking you about Hrasnica. Is it legitimate to carry out a counter-attack when, during the cease-fire, the Muslim Army from Hrasnica is, nevertheless, carrying out attacks? You did your service in the military. You should know whether this is legitimate.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps it is legitimate if only military targets are attacked.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Suljevic, just to clarify one thing, do you know where the Famos factory was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Was it or is it in the Hrasnica area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's the area of the municipality of Hrasnica, and it's separate from the civilian area. But it is in the area of the Hrasnica municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Suljevic. Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the line of separation went between the Famos factory and the rest of Hrasnica?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where the line was exactly, but it was somewhere around there. Now, was it all of Famos that was on one side or not, I'm not sure. But if the line did not go through Famos, then it went right by the factory, itself, as far as I know. And I don't really know because I was never there during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us focus on the last sentence now, please. What was it that General Milosevic ordered? Did he order fire or did he order readiness for the implementation of this task, and that he should be informed personally?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we have read it out already, that all preparations should be carried out, that a target should be selected, and that Commander Milosevic should be informed about all of that personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. However, on that day and on that occasion, was that bomb actually fired?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know what existed in Hrasnica as a military structure, as installations, positions, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I know that in Hrasnica, there was a unit of the BH Army. Now, I can't remember what its exact name was. Now, was it the 4th Company or Brigade, or -- I don't know what its name was. But I don't know about the details, anyway. A few times during the war, I did go there because my family, that is to say, my parents and my brother and sister are there, and a few times I just went to see them. But I didn't go towards the lines, and I don't know where things were, specifically.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you which heavy weaponry there was in Hrasnica?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know which weapons and artillery pieces were on Igman, right above Hrasnica? Rather, is Igman to the south of Hrasnica, right above Hrasnica, and is Hrasnica on the slopes where Igman rolls into the fields?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's true that Hrasnica is at the foot of Mount Igman. Now, I really don't know what it was that the Army of BH had either in Igman or elsewhere. I don't know. I mean, from the media, what I know to this day is what I found out just that way, through the media. I didn't know anything else.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now please ask for 1D02358 [as interpreted]. Could we have that in e-court, 1D20358, please. Could we now have ERN number 03315973-03319574.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Suljevic, while we're waiting for that, could you please have a look at this and tell us whether these are documents coming from your service? Are they the ones that are referred to in these tables?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so. Judging by the numbers, I think these are documents from our service.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we admit that previous document, General Milosevic's order, the one that we discussed? I don't know whether it's been admitted already.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that document is already in evidence as Exhibit P120.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Suljevic, could you read the title of this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "An Overview of a Part of Accounting Records in Sarajevo."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness please indicate where he's reading from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: He's reading from the document we are seeing at this moment. Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Just for clarification purposes, and perhaps it's not necessary, but the document, itself, I believe, is a document prepared by the Defence. I didn't know if the Court's call for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that's why I asked him to read it out. And he said that it's from his service, and I want that part to be clarified. But the title in e-court says it's a -- it says it's a review of Mr. Karadzic's Sarajevo reports. So if you could tell us what this document is about.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I said that this was from the service, I meant that the documents that are listed here under these numbers. But this particular document is not from our service, because I've never seen it before, this document I see on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If I may help, Mr. Suljevic, do you agree that this is an overview of documents emanating from your service?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me look at the numbers. 02/4-233, et cetera, yes, those are registration numbers from our service.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please focus your attention on the three columns on the right-hand side. It reads the registration number of the document, the date of entering the document in the log-book, and regularity of the entry. How was it possible that this one document has a smaller number than the previous one, but it comes after it? I mean, line 4 as compared to line 3, where we see the registration numbers. If we look at line 3, the date is 19 December 1994, and the one below is 5 June 1995, and yet it has a smaller number than the previous one.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see the problem. Numbers start from 1 every year, so for every year you start from 1. And depending on the number of documents received, will you get as far as you'll get, because in line 3 the document is from the previous year, and in line 4 it's from the following year. I don't see a problem with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. But still there is a muddle with these numbers. There's number 523, dated 10 July, on that line, and on the 10th line there's 531 from 3 July. How do you explain that?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's easy to explain. These are two entries that were completed in July, one on the 3rd and one on the 10th. They were received under these numbers stated here. We don't see the date of reception, but each entry is processed. And if two staff work on two files, two entries, then one may do the work sooner than the other.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the following page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Look at the boxes marked in red. All these dates are jumbled up. And what does this number 233 stand for, anyway? Because we see it in all years, this number 233. What does it mean?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are registration numbers in our office work. I'm not sure. "02/4" stands for the organisational unit, and "233" is some sort of classification. I'm not exactly sure what. But this is all about these matters, and that's why all are marked "233."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the following page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Take a look, and we can move on to page 4 and 5. Is it the same here?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the same, yes. There's no difference. These are registration numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But, Mr. Suljevic, this doesn't say the date of completion, but the date of the entry of the document, and it's such a muddle that your explanation can't really account for it, because we see here "Date of Entry." On this page, only three fit in some sort of chronological order. Let us see page 4. See, it's the same here. And let's see page 5 also, please.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but this document was not made by the same service that received and entered these documents, these files. I think that these are registration numbers, but the column that reads "Date of Entry of the Document in the Log-book," I think that these are actually the dates when the files were processed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, but -- that's what you think, but this was copied from the very documents, and it says when it was entered. So the first one was entered on the 22nd of September, 1995, under number 749, and number 751 was entered on the 13th of September. Well, all right. I'm satisfied with your explanation. I seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I wonder whether this is a proper document to be exhibited. Mr. Gaynor, do you have any observations?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Well, yes. I quite agree. First of all, it has been created by a member of the Defence team. As we've said before in respect of documents of this nature, we believe it would be more appropriate for them to be tendered through a Defence witness, who can then be cross-examined on the underlying data used to create the document in question. I'd also like to point out that this was made available to us this morning, and the cross-examination of this witness began on the 22nd of July, and we have not been provided with an English translation. But we'll leave it in the Court's discretion as to whether to admit it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You didn't have time to check whether all these numbers were correctly referenced?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: That's correct. We received it about half an hour before court started.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may assist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, you can use this as a kind of aide-memoir, but this is not the opportunity to tender this as a proper exhibit at this moment.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, I could have displayed all these documents and pointed out these discrepancies that way, but I don't have enough time. But I can call up any of these documents at random, so anyone may pick one and we can take a look at it. This is totally unacceptable, the way they do business there. It may be propaganda purposes, for war propaganda. But in criminal law, such jumbled dates really are intolerable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You'll have another opportunity to tender this as an exhibit. We'll do without it at this moment. Let's move on, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we please see 1D2194. I apologise. This was taken out of the indictment, so if there's enough time left, we'll deal with this incident, because it doesn't feature in the latest version of the indictment anymore. So we have to be economical and focus on what is in the indictment first. Could we please see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the incident in Mis Irbina, Mr. Suljevic?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what exactly you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The incident that happened on the 17th of June, 1995. I will make a reference to the table, but I believe there was only one on the 17th of June, 1995.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Without a report, I really cannot remember. There were many incidents on many dates. I don't remember everything.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see ERN 0213-5485, please. Perhaps this can assist: 1D02342, if we could see that. Possibly all this is already admitted as a P exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember this map, Mr. Suljevic? Do you remember this report, Mr. Suljevic?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just let me look at it. Could I please see the second page, too. It seems familiar, but just in case, I'd like to be sure.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us see the second page, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this report was drafted by Predrag Kurtes, as we can see here, so I was not involved in writing this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But it's a report from your service?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is a report from the CSB. Predrag Kurtes was at the CSB, I think. Our services' reports were very different. I remember this event, and we worked on it, but this wasn't our report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you work on this incident? Were you a team member, and if so, your name would be in first place?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did work on this event. I don't know about my name being in first place, but it doesn't matter. It is clear who conducted the on-site investigation. I was merely a team member.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In this event, which happened on 17 June, whereas the report was written on the 1st of July, one boy was killed and six more persons were injured. Out of six injured persons, five are children; correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see the previous document, where the map was. The previous document before this one, it was a map. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Suljevic, is this a map where we see the Mis Irbina Street in the center?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who was Mis Irbi [phoen] after whom this street was named?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I couldn't really say exactly, although I know it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Mis Irbi was a great British humanitarian worker who was with the Serbian Army throughout the First World War?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I guess.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What's the name of that street today?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it still has the same name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What is the relevance of these lines of questions? What is your question, Mr. Karadzic? You said that this incident had been taken out of the indictment, and you're coming back to this matter again. Move on to your -- what is your question?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dositejeva Street was renamed, or, rather, was taken out, but these very things that were taken out of the indictment strengthen the position of the Defence, and we must deal with them because these are examples of what should not have been done. And it all goes to show how the Serbian side was unjustly accused, and I cannot fail to mention this since one of my generals has been convicted already. And the relevance, Your Honours, is that mostly all streets in Sarajevo were renamed, to the detriment of cohabitation and coexistence. Serbian and Croatian personalities were all -- their names were all removed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you have the schedule number of this incident you are going to refer to, which allegedly took place on 17th of June?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the map has the number down here, and it's 1D --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I mean the schedule number of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll see in the table.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Gaynor, do you have --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: There might be some confusion. There was an incident on the 16th of June, 1995, at Dositejeva Street which has not been removed from the indictment. That's incident number 14 in Schedule G.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. So that was the reason why I asked the question. I don't see any incident which allegedly took place on the 17th of June.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we then now see 65 ter 09808.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document has been admitted as Exhibit P1327.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this document, Mr. Suljevic?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Suljevic, would you like to see the last page of this document, where your signature appears?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can have a look at it, Your Honours. But judging by the introduction, I remember this document and this incident as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Let's continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This was the incident in Dositejeva Street. Can you just briefly tell us what happened on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this incident, the Pomology Institute was hit by a modified aerial bomb, which exploded there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was your role in this examination?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was at the site in the status of an employee of the Counter-Sabotage Department. We were collecting what remained after the explosion. And then after on, I was involved in the expert analysis of the traces of the explosion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was the goal of this investigation? What were you supposed to establish?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just like in any other on-site investigation, we acted on the orders of the judge who was in charge of the on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was that a ballistic expert analysis or did you focus only on the consequences of the explosion, the damage and so on?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we from the KDZ, in general, did not deal with assessing the damage. That was not our main goal. Our goal was to analyse the crater, if we can call it that, because in this case the shell hit a wall, and also collecting traces. I'm not sure whether, in this specific instance, we also tried to establish the direction from which the projectile flew. We can only see that if I read through the entire document, because I cannot say this off the top of my head.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please provide this document to Mr. Suljevic? I have it here, so I can give him a hard copy, or perhaps we can move on to the next page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's sufficient if I just have a look at this document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you agree, I can provide a hard copy of this document to the witness, and we might show up 1D02194.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Unless the Prosecution opposes, I would like the witness to have the hard copy of this document, and we move on to another document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see 1D02194.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Parts of which motor did you find there? Was it Plamen?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We found three rocket projectiles of the Grad type, and calibre of 122 millimetres. And at the site, we also found the metal part of irregular shape, with the markings which you mentioned, and that's what's stated in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It's Plamen, the name of the motor is Plamen, which means "flame"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three rocket projectiles of the Grad type were found, and one metal part, which is mentioned in the report, most probably was not part of the device that exploded. And I can explain that, in a way, because people in Sarajevo used to collect these parts as souvenirs. Even journalists did that, and I don't know whoever else. Quite often, people would collect the parts which they found someplace, and they would keep them as mementos or souvenirs of a kind. And it says here that this part most probably was not part of the device that fell.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us try to be more specific. Who conducted the on-site investigation and who collected the fragments?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I participated in the work of the team which collected the traces.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When did that take place; how long after the explosion?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly how long after the explosion, but probably you can see from the CSB report when it took place. I just know that I was not at the official premises. I was at home, as far as I can remember this incident, and they called me to come there. I thought it -- I think it was one of the days of a weekend and that I came to the on-site investigation from my home. But how long after the explosion it was, I couldn't specifically say, because I cannot remember such details.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What did you find there? Was the site properly secured for the forensic examination?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who did you find at the site? What did you find there when you got there?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you couldn't find anyone at such sites. When shelling was in progress, you couldn't find anyone there who was not there because of their duty. I don't have the report here, which would show whom we found there and whom was at the site. And from this point in time, I cannot remember every incident and every on-site investigation and who was involved, because the personnel in teams changed. It was not always the same people, always the same investigating judge and so on. So from this point in time, I cannot remember such details without reviewing certain documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, this was a major incident, wasn't it? What is the name of the street now? Can you please mark on this map Dositejeva Street?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can mark the street, but whether it has retained the name or not, I really wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Am I right that it is the street which is the continuation of Djuro Djakovic Street, that is to say, Kralja Tomislava, the name of which was changed and it's now called Kosevo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will mark approximately where I believe that the street is. It's not the street up there you mentioned. Dositejeva Street is, I believe, here [marks]. I think there or thereabouts is Dositejeva Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. So we see that the BiH Railway Company is there, so is the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the vicinity, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And do you know where the command of the helicopter unit on Dositejeva Street was?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't even know that there was a helicopter squadron, to be honest, so I couldn't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The explosion was at 4A, and the command of the squadron was at 4. That's the neighbouring building; correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I know where the explosion occurred, but where the command was situated, I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right, thank you. How did you enter the street? From which end of the street did you come to the site?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. I think you can reach the site from four sides; that is to say, from two sides of the street once you enter the street. And I don't remember how I entered the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And where did you live?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I lived in Cengic Vila.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You came by car, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I cannot remember whether I came on foot or whether someone came to pick me up. I really don't remember such details. I did not record that, I did not keep a diary, so I cannot answer such questions. It's possible that I got there by car. I really don't know how important that is in this context.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please allow for the possibility that it's very important for the Defence. Cengic Vila is about four kilometres away from this place, is that correct, if not more?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible, because from work we usually needed 50 to 60 minutes to arrive, though sometimes we would need up to three hours due to shelling. So, more or less, it was like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So we have to assume that you did not come to the on-site investigation, this incident, on foot, but, rather, by car; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not certain how I got there, so I wouldn't --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, and at what time did the explosion occur?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As one can see from the report, the projectile hit at about 11.05 a.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And when did you arrive there?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I've told you. I don't know when I got there, but the on-site investigation was conducted on that same day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Ah-hah. And now please tell us, once you got there, what did you find there? Did anyone else come to the site before you? I'm not talking about the public, about people, but someone was doing something there. Who did you find on the spot when you got there?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I have answered that question. I cannot remember all the people who were members of the on-site investigation team, or whom I found on the spot, or who arrived there after me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you were certainly involved in the on-site investigation; correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you collected the fragments of the projectile which were found after the explosion; correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was involved in collecting the traces. And I remember that there was another colleague of mine there who was a member of the Counter Sabotage Protection from my department within the CSB.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please mark, with numbers, the BiH Railway Company with number 1, and the Presidency with number 2, and the Ministry of the Foreign Affairs with number 3?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's written here on the map. You can see the BH Railway Company, number 1. [Marks]. Here it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the Presidency?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here's the Presidency. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the Ministry of the Foreign Affairs?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Suljevic. It was because we couldn't read in the Bosnian. But did they exist at the time, i.e., in 1995, at the same place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours, they existed there at the time, and they are still there now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please write the date and your signature or your initials. And I would tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What you encircled here, is that the site of the explosion? So that we can be a bit more specific, can you please put number 4 there. That's 4A. I think the name of the street is Branislav Djurdjev now, and it used to be Dositejeva Street; correct? Can we please return to the screen what Mr. Suljevic signed so that he can add number 4 to the exact site where the explosion occurred?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It won't be necessary, because well aware of the marking where it is. And then with the comments of the witness, another marking of the number won't be necessary. We'll admit it as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D552, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And we can move on, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree, Mr. Suljevic -- actually, can we just keep the map a little longer? Is the regional SUP there as well? That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. The CSB is there. But just a small correction. I think that the street is a bit to the right, if I can mark it with the red marker. Perhaps I did not place Dositejeva correctly. I think it was towards the left a bit more, towards the cinema called Dubrovnik before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do we agree that Dositejeva is moving from north to south, not the other way around?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]. The Institute of Pomology, or whatever it was called, is there as I marked it. Now, as for Dositejeva, whether that runs from north to south, I really don't know. I mean, it's no problem to check that on maps that were contemporaneous.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you live in Sarajevo for a long time?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Doesn't Dositejeva link Marsal Tita and Mis Irbina?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I don't know where it started and where it ended; Dositejeva Street, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that within this complex that you marked just now, there are no residential buildings? This is a bank, the Dubrovnik Cinema, then the old Austrian building of the railways, then the Foreign Ministry, the Regional Centre of Security?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And then after the CSB, there is a series of residential buildings towards Mis Irbina and that entire area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What you marked with red, there is no residential building there; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether there are any residential areas there. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Let's use the same number so that we know exactly where the site of the explosion was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I wonder whether we can keep this new map and admit it, keep it as D552. So we replace the previous D552 with this one. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The CSB is there on the corner of Mis Irbina and August Cerares. I guess August Cerares did something wrong, too, so he lost his street as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It's called Musala now; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The CSB is now in the street called La Benevolencije. I really have no idea what it was called before the war. The CSB is nearby, and that's that street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: La Benevolencije, yes, and it used to be Augusta Cerares. Right. Now, do you recall that during the NATO bombing of Serbia, NATO hit practically all the government buildings of Serbia at the time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, I'll withdraw it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How was it that you determined the direction from which this modified aerial bomb, as the reports call it, came?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this case, what was taken into account was the position of the remnants of the rocket motors that remained in the wall at the site of the explosion. The wall had been hit from the northern side. The building was hit on its northern side, rather, so that's the side that was affected.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do we have a photograph? Did you take any photographs there?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't take any photographs. There was a member of the team whose task that was, and I think that the site was photographed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you have that photograph? Do we have that photograph?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a question for the Registry, why we lost the red markings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll bring up the new marking -- D552 with the red marking.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] While we're waiting for all of that:

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Suljevic, did you determine the angle of decent of that projectile? You know which side of the building was affected. However, did you determine the angle of decent of the projectile?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not determine the angle of decent of the projectile at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you need that? What were you able to conclude on that basis, in view of the fact that you did not have the angle of descent?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We could conclude what the approximate direction was from which the projectile had come. As far as aerial bombs are concerned, modified aerial bombs that fell on the city, well, we didn't have any tables and we didn't have the resources. Even if we wanted to, we could not determine the angle of descent. I don't think there would have been any point in doing that in the case of these modified aerial bombs that were rocket-propelled.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you know what the mass of the projectile was or of the warhead? How heavy was it?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, in this case we did not actually establish which aerial bomb that was. We couldn't do that. So the report says that it is most probably an aerial bomb, so this modified aerial bomb was probably the mechanism that was involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What bomb could this have been, according to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can just guess now. What we established at the time on the spot is what is recorded in our reports. Was it -- if it were possible to determine it then, it would have been in our reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So what was possible, 100 kilograms, 250 kilograms; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 100 kilograms and 250 kilograms. We saw that in those orders where modified aerial bombs were referred to, and launchers as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, tell us, you established the approximate location from which the projectile had been fired; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not establish the approximate location. We established the direction, and that's what the report says, that the direction coincides with the direction in which the enemy positions are in Pionirska Dolina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I see. So it was only Serb positions in Pionirska Dolina? Weren't there Muslim positions only 50 metres away from them?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The separation lines were somewhere in Pionirska Dolina. I don't know. I don't know what you're getting at, what it is you want to define specifically.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We want to specify how it was that you determined the distance. You don't know the angle of descent, you don't know so many other factors, and you determined the actual distance involved. In that area, Pionirska Dolina, towards the north, it goes all the way to Tuzla, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not establish the distance. We said that this direction from which the projectile came coincides with the direction of enemy positions in the broader area of Pionirska Dolina. It coincides with that, with that locality. It doesn't say what the distance was. It wasn't determined, it wasn't measured. And we know where state -- how big it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When you say "Pionirska Dolina," you're not saying only what the direction is, but you're saying what the distance is, too; right? Why not between Pionirska Dolina and the actual site, along the same axis, couldn't it have been fired from somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The direction coincides with that locality and from the site where the projectile fell, so, I mean, that's the trajectory that the projectile took.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm afraid that the transcript does not reflect that they did not establish the mass of the bomb and so on. This is LiveNote, so I hope that my fast speech will be corrected during the night.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So all these conclusions, do they coincide with what you had established? From Pionirska Dolina, did anyone else determine anything else?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether anyone else carried out investigations, besides us. But I say, once again, that it says here that the direction of firing coincides with that locality where enemy positions were in the broader area of Pionirska Dolina. There is no specific reference to where it had been fired from, but I'm sure that it's from that locality that it was fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How can you be certain of that?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that is confirmed by the orders that we saw during the previous two days of my testimony, where there is constant repetition of launchers being made and these modified aerial bombs being made. I don't know of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina having a single one of those, at least within the Sarajevo theatre of operations. As for these modified aerial bombs, I first saw them inactivated or, rather, ready during reintegration at Zeljezara Ilijas, a photograph, rather, because our teams went to different locations after the Dayton Agreement had been signed. And within reintegration, we were carrying out preparations, and, if necessary, we were removing mines, explosive devices, and the like, so that the inhabitants could return to their homes safely. I saw these modified air bombs on the photographs that were in Zeljezara Ilijas. There were metal barrels, 200-litres metal barrels full of explosive, and tyres from freight vehicles had been mounted on them. They were used in order to get these mechanisms down from the hills and activated somewhere in town.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So the Serbs did that. They would fill a barrel with explosive and then let it roll downhill; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is what was found in Zeljezara Ilijas that throughout the war was under the control of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was it a possibility that they were captured from the Muslim Army, and do you know that the Muslim Army used that from Igman when attacking Serb houses? We'll find a document to that effect here. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that, but I know that in Sarajevo there were cases that such things had exploded somewhere above Bistrik, and the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina certainly couldn't have rolled them uphill.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Although they had sophisticated artillery, the Serbs used these barrels; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you are asking for my opinion --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you trying to say that the Muslim Army in Sarajevo had no modified aerial bombs? Just yes or no, that's easy.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the answer is no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What does this mean, "100 kilograms and 250 kilograms"?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're referring to aerial bombs, I think it is the total mass of the bomb.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What is the weight of the explosive therein?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know exactly what the mass of the explosive is there, but, say, 30 to 40 per cent. However, there is data in literature. I cannot say now exactly. I think that an air-bomb of 250 kilograms has about 100 kilograms of explosive, perhaps a bit less. But, tentatively, say it's about 100 kilograms.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: 100 kilograms of TNT, what kind of damage does that inflict on buildings or wherever it may fall, Mr. Suljevic?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it depends on the place where it falls. Every situation is different. It depends on what the building had been made of, where the projectile exploded. There are many factors involved, so it is hard to give a specific answer to your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Where did this one explode, on which wall, and what was the damage inflicted?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What kind of damage it inflicted you can see on the photo documentation. I think that the wall was a brick wall. I don't know. I cannot remember now. But we can only see that in the photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you do recall, on the spot, what was it, what was the debris? Was it bricks or was it reinforced concrete? Wasn't that an old Austrian building?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It certainly wasn't reinforced concrete, but I cannot remember from this time distance. That was not the only on-site investigation that I carried out during the war. Perhaps I would not remember anything, given the time that has elapsed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us be serious and precise, Mr. Suljevic. 100 kilograms of TNT falls on a building that was made of bricks. What kind of damage is inflicted? What happens when a 100 -- when a bomb of 100 kilograms of TNT falls on that building? What was it that you found there once you came?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, you are saying that this air-bomb is of 250 kilograms, containing 100 kilograms of explosive, but the report does not show that at all, that it was 250 kilograms. It was either 100 kilograms or 250. The report does not say specifically. However, the destruction there was vast, and you can see that in the photo documentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Give us this photo documentation. Can the OTP give us this photo documentation? The transcript does not reflect that you could not establish which bomb it was. However, you do agree that there are no aerial bombs that are lighter than 100 kilograms; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that there are any that are lighter. Without referring to literature, I cannot say anything with 100 per cent certainty. Perhaps those were the smallest aerial bombs that existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You state in your report that it had three rocket engines of the Grad type. Can we please see 65 ter 09808 on our screens. That's the report, but you have it in front of you anyway. Is it true that you state there that three rocket motors of the Grad type were found there? How did you arrive at that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's stated in the report remains of a rocket motor, that is, tubes, found at the site.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Which pieces are required to establish the number of motors?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The bodies of the motors don't get destroyed in the explosion. They can be found at the site only damaged or deformed. Only at the RTV Centre; we didn't find any at the site. Probably the rocket motor got separated from the aerial bomb, itself, during its trajectory.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, that would have been a unique instance. You said to us that it happened when it ricochetted off that roof?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I thought, and that's why I said it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You know why you found those pieces from the RTV Centre? You found them in Safeta Hadzica, because it landed there, but we cannot leave this so messy and unexplained. Is it correct that you needed three vital parts of any motor to be able to establish that there were indeed three motors? There must be three jets, twelve wings, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can we see the part which is referring to what you just said, motors of Grad type? What page is it?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here on page 1, if I may assist. It says four large metal tubes were found, seven large metal pieces of irregular shape.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What are these four large metal parts? Are these four motors?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On page 2, there is a description of the parts. They are marked by numbers, and then their dimensions are stated, as established by measuring, and some characteristic traces visible on the parts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you found four, and you say that there were three motors. And one of these motors belonged to Plamen, correct, according to you? I mean, that's what your report says.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it says so in the report, then that's the way it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So three motors would propel the bomb, and the fourth motor would belong to a Plamen missile; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fourth wasn't a Grad motor, because those parts were found at the site.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us look at paragraph 3 on page 1. You say here -- but it may be on page 2, after all. You say here that the missiles were used to propel it, to propel the whole thing? Actually, it's on page 2, paragraph 3.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the last page, it says that the missiles were used to propel the bomb. It's on page 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Then do you -- would you say that missiles and rocket motors are the same thing? Because it says here that missiles were used to propel the bomb.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, rocket motors.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But read all of this: "Based on the material brought for forensic analysis." Who brought it?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The material was collected at the site and taken to the CSB. Their requests for forensic analysis were filed, and these were attached to material from the site. No matter whether somebody from our department conducted the on-site investigation, with the request to conduct forensic analysis, traces had to be attached.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you did that?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I took part in collecting evidence. That's what I said earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now take a look at the following paragraph: "A metal fragment of irregular shape ..."

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "A metal fragment of irregular shape with the stamped mark, 128 millimetres, M63 and BK comes from the exhaust duct of a 128-millimetre Plamen M-63 missile, which most probably was not a part of the device that exploded."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But what was that motor doing there? It's part of a missile; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I explained that. At the site, there were also pieces of other projectiles, things people left there, souvenirs and the like.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could it have belonged to some military facility or military unit of the Muslim Army there in that street?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There, in that institute, most certainly not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you want to hear what I think, Mr. Suljevic? I think that no aerial bomb ever flew to Dositejeva Street, number 4, although that's an area full of legitimate targets. And the neighbouring building housed the command of the helicopter squadron of the Muslim Army, but, Mr. Suljevic, even if there was only 100 kilograms of TNT there, the whole building would have been blown to pieces. But I don't understand how they made you draw such conclusions to establish even the direction and the distance from which it had come based on totally unclear elements from which nothing can be concluded, and we don't even have a photograph.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing is unclear here. What is stated in our reports is not unclear. Never, during my work in on-site investigations or forensic analyses, did I put on paper anything that I haven't seen or that I wasn't certain of. Never did I receive instructions from anybody to put on paper something I wasn't certain of and that couldn't be proved. Nobody, to this day, instructed me to say something behind -- to say anything to which I wouldn't stand.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was there a fire there?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But wasn't there -- wasn't there the mark for "inflammable" on the jet of that device?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. But if I did say so, then I stand by that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, I seem to be too fast for the transcript, but I want to finish today. I would like your statement given on 19 June 1995 to be referred to in the transcript, where you say that the Plamen exhaust jet was marked "flammable."

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that is stated in the report, then I stand by that. But if it isn't stated in the report, then it isn't that way. But I cannot see the report now, so I cannot confirm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, since you know about these things: Where is the "flammable" mark placed, and how is it applied; by stamping, by colour? And where is it placed, on the motor or on the warhead?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, and what I am about to say doesn't refer to aerial bombs or modified aerial bombs, with rocket motors to propel them, but on artillery shells the marks are applied by painting them, and I believe that in the Eastern Bloc, in the arsenal of the former JNA, a red band meant flammable, whereas a yellow band meant chemical missile. I don't think that NATO has the same system of markings. But I didn't prepare for this line of questioning, so I didn't consult the relevant literature, but there are books where that can be found. When we speak about marking ammunition, we relied on the textbooks of the Military Technical Academy in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. I note the time is time to break, but before we do: Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. A few lines ago, the accused said -- referred to part of the report of the 19th June 1995, and he said that there was a reference to a marking of "flammable" on the Plamen rocket. I request the accused to direct us to the paragraph he's referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After the break, if I may. I now have just another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who manufactured a Plamen missile with flammable heads in Bosnia? Because you'll agree with me that the other Plamen missiles were not flammable and that only certain special versions were flammable and who made them in Bosnia-Herzegovina? Do you agree with me when I say it was a Soko Mostar?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know what Soko manufactured and what Pretis did. I really don't know. But in the former Yugoslavia, there were industries manufacturing such projectiles. But where exactly, what type was manufactured, I don't know. I worked for the Zrak company, which didn't manufacture projectiles, so I don't know. I don't know which factory exactly manufactured what.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We will continue after the break, because were must clarify what happened in Dositejeva Street, because what is stated in the indictment never happened, Mr. Suljevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's your statement, Mr. Karadzic. We'll break for half an hour and resume at five past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. If I could just let you know that Dr. Subotic, who's been assisting us as an expert, is present and will continue to be assisting Dr. Karadzic during this testimony. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We noted it. Thank you. Yes, Mr. Karadzic, let's continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I need to discuss at least two other incidents with this witness, as there is no better witness than this one I can discuss that with, because he was involved in them. One of them is in the indictment; that's the flea market. And the other one is not in the indictment, but it has been admitted as P and some number, all the documents. I really don't know the exact number now, so we really have to review all that. And I would ask you to consider allowing me sufficient time to discuss this incident as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Suljevic, let us just briefly conclude with the incident in Dositejeva Street. You concluded that it had to be a Serbian shell because the Muslim Army did not have modified bombs; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not what the report says, but I will now state my opinion. This is so, and there is no doubt that these aerial bombs were launched by the Army of Republika Srpska, whose supreme commander you were. This was also confirmed by all the orders which we saw on the previous two days of my testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking you that. We will establish that. But did you found your claim, that it's indubitable that it was the Army of Republika Srpska, on the basis of the fact that the Muslims did not have modified aerial bombs and that Serbs were in Pionirska Dolina, and what else were the grounds for such a conclusion?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said the report does not say whose bombs these were, but I have stated my opinion after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Ah-hah. So you could not establish what kind of bomb it was, 100 or 150 kilos. It was probably not 500 kilos. You could not establish whose it was. You are stating your opinion, and you say that only Serbian positions were on this direction; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you are not precise, so it's not exactly as you just stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, on the basis of what do you claim that this was a Serbian bomb, when you couldn't establish in the report that it was?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The bombs that fell on the city of Sarajevo, it's well known where they fell from, all of them, both artillery projectiles and bombs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you concluded it on the basis of that. Was it on the basis of that that you decided what was falling on Sarajevo had to be a Serbian bomb; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We cannot speculate here or offer theses. One projectile cannot be both launched and explosions staged in the same place, just like with the bomb on the RTV Centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Suljevic, I'm asking you this: During the on-site investigation, you could not establish what kind of bomb it was or where it came from, but you concluded that it could have come from Pionirska Dolina because Serbs were there. But Muslims were also in Pionirska Dolina, 50 metres away from the Serbs. I'm asking you this: Judging by certain circumstances, you concluded that this was a Serbian bombs, because the Muslims did not have such bombs and because what was falling on Sarajevo were Serbian bombs? Yes or no, and then we'll move on.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You want me to say that all bombs and all projectiles which did not have any effect on the target, in the sense that they wounded or killed someone, that they were launched by you and your army, and whenever there were any victims, that we were the ones who launched it against ourselves. That's absurd.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us not enter into a debate. Your conclusion was that the Serbs had that, that they were in Pionirska Dolina, and that what was falling on Sarajevo was launched by Serbs. Do you have anything more specific than that on the basis of which you concluded it was a Serb bomb?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we take as our position the report, whatever is in the report was concluded at the on-site investigation and it was like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us leave aside the report. I'm asking you now, here in the courtroom, on the basis of which do you conclude it was a Serb bomb? Was it anything exact or were these the reasons that you just stated that led you to conclude that it was a Serbian-launched bomb?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, look, I'm now certain that these were the bombs which were launched from the positions of the Army of Republika Srpska. And what convinced us that it was so were also the orders issued by the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us leave that aside now. On the basis of which did you establish, for this specific bomb, which allows you to claim that it was launched by the Serbs? On the basis of what?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me not repeat. Just like with all other bombs, this is my opinion, and the report does not state whose bomb it was. There is not a single report that says whose projectile it was, but what's written there is so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, thank you. Please tell us another thing. Do you make a difference between a motor and a projectile?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a distinction should be made between a motor, which is a propelling agent and propelling part, and the projectile. It should be distinguished.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What is the distinction?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the assembly of a rocket includes the head, with the charge, and the propelling part.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So when you say it's a projectile, then it has the motor and it also has the warhead; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be better to say that it's a rocket.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How many statements did you give since 1995? We are still searching for a document which says that you saw that it said "inflammable." How many statements did you give in 1995?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how many statements I have given so far. I really don't remember, but I always responded to the call of the Prosecutor whenever I was requested to give a statement. I do not remember that I ever said that it was an inflammable projectile. But as I said a while ago, I stand by all my reports and what they contain, if it is properly translated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But do you agree that if you saw that there was the word "inflammable" on a projectile, that then it had to be the warhead, because such a word would not be placed on the motor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in general, only warheads are marked in this way, depending on the type of projectile and the type of charge which the projectile contains.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll move to the next incident, the flea market the 22nd of December, 1994. Are you familiar with this incident?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. President, before we move to the next incident, I'd just like to clarify one matter for the record. Mr. Karadzic, before the break, said: "I would like your statement given on 19th June 1995 to be referred to in the transcript, where you say that the Plamen exhaust jet was marked 'flammable.'" Now, that's a clear reference to P1237, which is the report of this incident drafted by the witness concerning this incident. That report does not contain -- that statement, I understood, Mr. Karadzic was going to make that absolutely clear on the record, and we ask him to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, you promised to come back to that point, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps just the date was wrong. It was not necessarily the 19th of June, which is my birthday, but probably some other date. But it's quite certain that in one of the statements from that period, Mr. Suljevic said that in Dositejeva he saw the word "inflammable," and we will obtain that; not in this statement, but in some other documents. We're trying to locate the specific document that contains this reference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You need to give us a specific reference by the end of this session. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. My associates will try to locate the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Suljevic, do you remember this incident which occurred on the 22nd of December, 1994, at the flea market?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you participate in the investigations?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did the incident occur at 9.10 in the morning?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that's what the report says, then it was so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It's G9 from the table, from Table G, Incident 9.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The time when the projectile fell and exploded were established at the site by interviewing witnesses, because we didn't know when which projectile fell. We would establish that once we came to the scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When did you come out to the scene?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once again, it's the same question as the one you asked me before the break. I think that you should take all the documents which relate to this incident, and whatever they contain is correct. Once again, I don't remember when we would arrive to the scene. In one of the CSB reports, it should say at what time the on-site investigation began. We did not do that because we were the Counter-Sabotage Department and we conducted the on-site analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is nothing against you, personally, Mr. Suljevic. I'm interested in what it looks like when we do not rely on 92 ter and statements, but your testimony. You are a witness here. You were there. What was the time when you came out to the scene?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the call from CSB, we came out to the scene and we joined the on-site investigation team.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was that at 10.00, 11.00, or 12.00? When was that?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know when it was. It's possible -- it couldn't have been at 12.00. It was probably earlier than that. But from this distance in time, I don't know who could remember whether he came out to the scene at a specific time, because such incidents occurred practically on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, do you have any notes that could serve as an aide-memoire? Did you use any notes in your work?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we did not keep a diary, or a log, or any sort of notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Ah-hah, all right. Can you tell us, what was the weather like that morning?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember what the weather was like. I know that there was no precipitation, but what it was like, whether it was cloudy or not, I can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was the visibility like?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I also cannot remember what the visibility was like, whether it was good or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, we both used to live in Sarajevo. We know what sort of weather you normally get in Sarajevo in December.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
