utterances.text: In Sarajevo in December, when it's calm, then it's usually foggy, but when it's windy, then it's clear. So on that specific date, I don't remember what it was like, and I cannot rely on the general assumption about what the weather is usually like and then claim that the weather was like that on that specific day. At least I cannot do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. There are many things you don't remember, Mr. Suljevic, and that would be of great help for us. I will recall you that in the trial of General Milosevic, Witness W-12 testified that it was foggy. How come that you don't remember that it was foggy?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fog wasn't so thick that I would remember it. I'm certain that it wasn't the Sarajevo fog from before the war, when you couldn't see a thing. I think that the visibility was relatively good.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we please look at 13172. That's 65 ter 13172.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On the second page, that's ERN 102-5464, can you please have a look at the second paragraph, line 16. I think there's been a confusion with the ERN numbers. I have established that in many of the searches, the ERN is 102-5464. Is this 65 ter 13172? Yes, now we have the version in Serbian. This is the statement of Salih Djedovic, but in English we do not have the right document. Could I please ask you to read outline 16 from the second paragraph?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Line 16, you mean, from the title "Statement," and then the 16th line?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "... which hit -- caused by a shell, which hit the window of a privately-owned shop in Petra Kocic Street across the street from the market." Is this what you mean? "The explosion of the second shell caused the confusion and screams among the citizens to increase at the market, and soon the employees of the market and then also members of the police and members of the Army of BH came to assist the wounded. After the explosion of the second shell, I started in the direction of the place where the shells fell, and the distance between the places where the first and the second shell was around 10 metres." Should I go on reading?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And what was the time between the fall of the first and second shell? Does the report contain that or did you note that in the report?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not. I and my colleagues who worked on this did not establish how much time elapsed between the two shells. Perhaps that is contained in some report, but I don't know what the situation was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you establish that the first shell fell in the shop window?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Look, when we came to the scene, we found two craters there. The only thing that can be established on the basis of witness statements is which one was the first to fall and which one was the second to fall. So if it says here the first one fell in the shop window, and after that the second one, that's the way it was, but that is based on the statement of the person who made the statement. I cannot assert now whether that statement made by that person is correct or not, and I do not wish to do that. And I cannot say which shell fell first, the first one or the second one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But this is an eye-witness though, and he says the first shell fell into the shop window. How do you establish that?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not that the shell fell into the shop window. It fell in front of the wall of some shop, some craftsman's shop.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now, let us see whether you find this a bit strange, that the police and the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina just happened to be there all at the same time and all at once.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not like to comment on this statement made by this person who made the statement. I mean, what does that mean, "members of the police" and "members of the army"? Does it mean one, does it mean ten, does it mean an entire brigade? I really wouldn't want to comment on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this statement part of your investigation material in respect of this incident?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have seen the statement. And as I said, I accept all the statements that I saw, I accept them as such, because it is only the person who gave the statement that stands by these statements. As a matter of fact, even the person who took the statement cannot stand by the information provided in the statement. In this particular case, it was Curevac. It is only the person who actually made the statement who stands by the information provided in the statement. We can only accept it or not accept it as such.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have 103541. That is a sketch of the scene.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just before we move on, I note this is page 70 of that document, and what we see in English seems to be a partial translation thereof. Can you confirm that, Mr. Gaynor?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Page 70 seems to be the page in Serbian. The English translation has only 32 pages, compared to the 92 pages -- 91 pages of the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I understand the difference in the number of pages may be because the English translation contains translations of a number of the originals on one English page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. So for the purpose of future reference, you need to indicate the e-court page numbers, Mr. Karadzic. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have this ERN number, 102-5411. It's the same document, but it is 5411. That's the page number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Page 17, I take it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I do apologise. We are short of human resources. We don't have enough people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, the Registry has set up various regimes to help you, and you have a lot of associates. I don't like to hear that complaint again. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not a complaint. I'm grateful. Can you imagine how hard it would be had they not made these improvements? We wouldn't have been able to do a thing. Can we have that sketch, the one that was on the screen a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Page 18. This is page 18, and now we are seeing page 17.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Suljevic, are you familiar with this sketch?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw it in the previous period. I'm not the author.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you mark on this sketch the locations where the persons who had lost their lives were?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't do it without a legend. And I think that those locations are actually marked. As I said a moment ago, we had no way of knowing when the projectiles fell, and, therefore, we could not know when persons died. That was established on the basis of statements or, rather, on the basis of the locations where the corpses were found. When we came to the scene, we did not find scenes on this location. They had already been removed, both the wounded persons and the corpses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did anyone register where these people were hit, where they died, and where they were wounded? Did anyone mark these places?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This sketch should have a legend of its own, and we will see what is marked by the numbers that we see here on the sketch. Numbers 1 through 30, it seems. We should see the legend, and then that will show what is denoted by each and every number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So you do not have your own independent knowledge where the dead people were or as to this map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have that knowledge, Your Honour, but I can assume, on the basis of this sketch, that number 8 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: There's no point of asking those questions to this witness. Let's --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the previous page, please, so this one and the previous one. On the previous one, we can see the legend, so then let us help Mr. Suljevic help us understand what it was that happened here or what is claimed to have happened here. The previous one with the legend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Page 16.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have pages 16 and 17 together on the screen. No, we don't need the English one. We need the sketch and we need the Serbian text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Well, then we can print out this 16 and hand it over to the witness, and we can see if we can the sketch at the same time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would appreciate that. Could page 17 be on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it easier for you now, Mr. Suljevic, to tell us what is on this sketch?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please do that, then?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm sure, and I assert and I saw that 1 and 2 -- actually, I agree with that 100 per cent, that those are the craters where the two projectiles fell. One is in front of the wall of the shop window, of some shop there, and the other one is on the pavement, marked number 2. And then I can continue along with this legend. 3 and 4 are the locations where two fragments were, probably of the projectiles. Then 5 and 8 are pools of blood. Number 7 is a shopping bag of one of the injured persons. Number 9 is part of the fuse of the projectile; that is to say, the place where that happened to be. Then 06 and 30 are also fragments of the projectile. 10 and 11, again, places where fragments of the projectile were. Then 12 is a lamp post, and 13 is a landmark from which you can see how far away the crater is. And it says here "Landmark, corner of the house in Oprkanj Street."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It used to be called Danila Ilica or Petar Kocic; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: One was called Danila Ilica and the other one was Petar Kocic, but they poor souls did something wrong and they lost their streets.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't want to go into a debate of these street names.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, their mistake was that they were Serbs. One was a great Bosnian writer, Serbian, Petar Kocic, and the other one belonged to the Young Bosnian Movement. All right, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You can't complain about the shortage of time at all, wasting your time on these subjects. What is your next question?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it took five seconds to say what I said about the street name, Excellency.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right now. Did anyone die in this incident?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there were some fatalities. The report says exactly how many.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Two persons; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. It says here two persons were killed on this occasion and several persons were wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Where is that marked?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Numbers 5 and 8 denote the pools of blood. Again, I don't want to speculate, but then there is a contour of a person here that is marked on the sketch, so I assume that that is one of the persons who was killed. But, again, that can be established through the witnesses there, the persons who removed those persons, I mean, during the explosions. That's the way it happened. That's how things happened. I mean, I don't really see what you're getting at. What are you trying to get at, where the person was, 20 metres, and then, say -- a person would be 20 metres away and get killed, and another person would be 5 metres away and only be injured. I really don't want to go into a discussion of this kind, because discussions like this lead us nowhere, and we cannot draw any conclusions, and, well --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Suljevic, this is a criminal investigation. This is a matter of criminal law. Two persons were killed, several were wounded. Why is that not marked on this sketch? How can we establish how it was that they got killed and injured, or are we supposed to take the word of someone? This criminal investigation was carried out in a sloppy way, and it cannot be used in this court or in any other court, for that matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't understand how this witness would be able to answer that question. Ask relevant questions which the witness is able to answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Suljevic, is there a better, more accurate, more proper investigation than this one? Do you have anything else?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can testify about what I did, and I can confirm what I know and what I saw and what I did on the scene. I am not the author of this sketch. As I said, I can confirm with 100 per cent certainty from this sketch the place where the two projectiles fell. That much I do know, because that happened to be there on the scene when we came to carry out the on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Suljevic, you came to testify about some incidents in whose investigations you participated. One of these, for which the Serb side is being blamed, is this particular incident. Please help us clarify this part of the indictment that the Serbian side is being charged with. You were part of that team. Please tell us where these persons were, what happened, so that we can establish beyond a reasonable doubt, yes, this is what happened, and then we are going to find out who it was that fired those shells. This way, please tell me just where these dead persons were lying and also where the wounded persons were here. Tell me that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: As we heard, this witness does not know that. There's no point repeating the same question. It's simply a waste of time. Move on to your next question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have a page from this document, ERN 10 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: It was too fast for interpretation.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know -- it's a photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What's the ERN number again? Not exactly ERN, but --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 102-53 -- or, rather, 5434 -- 25434, that's it. Page 40 of this document. Excellencies, the electronics seem to be way too slow. We can see that here. And also while I'm preparing for this, it is horrendously slow.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see this image, and is it familiar?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As it says down here underneath the photograph, this is a cover -- a protective cover where you can see damage sustained due to the explosion. However, what we can see here on this photograph, actually, it's barely noticeable, it's blurred, but we do see the damage on the cover or shutter. This is the wall on one of the shops that were there in a single line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So what do you infer on the basis of this photograph?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What should I infer, except for what is written under the photograph, that there is visible damage to the shutter, damaged caused by the fragments of a projectile?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us now take a look at the panoramic photograph of the site, DSCN -- just a minute. 1D02187. 1D02187. Here in this photograph, while we still see it, can you see some circles marked with chalk on the shutter?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this photograph, I see damages. Whether or not they are marked by chalk, I don't know, but there are some lighter portions.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we see the entire panoramic photograph?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise this location? Is this the site of the incident?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this is a postwar photograph. Yes, I think this is the site. I think this is the site. I can see the sign "Hotel." After the war, a hotel was opened here which wasn't there before the war. This could be the place. I don't see the tram line up there, but it should be somewhere by those buildings in the rear?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you mark the exact site of the incident here?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the projectiles, hereabouts [marks]. There was a curb at the time here. It's been changed since. And the other place of impact was hereabouts [marks] towards the tram line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But where's the tram line?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if this is the place, then this is the tram line towards Bascarsija [marks], if this is the site. It looks like it, but I said that I can't see the tram line. If it's there, then the rails should be there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could it be another place? We can see the mosque as an important landmark, so was this the flea market where the incident happened?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the plateau [marks]. Let's take it -- let's assume that this was the place, and then here there was the flea market [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please mark it 1, 2 and 3; 1 and 2 being the places of impact and 3 being the plateau.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1 [marks] is the place of impact somewhere in front of a wall by a shop. I cannot mark it accurately. Number 2 [marks] is the second crater, the impact of the other projectile. 3 [marks] is the plateau where there was a flea market. It may extend into the foreground. And the arrow marks the position of the tram line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please date it and sign it.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And, Mr. Suljevic, you're confident this is the site which that incident -- where the incident took place? We can keep it for the moment, and can we go back to page 17 of the previous document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We keep it. Yes, we admit it as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D553.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Page 17 of the previous document, which appears to have the note of a tram line and some further space, and then whether you can confirm that this is consistent with the picture. Page 17 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If this is what we see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you see the sketch on the left side? We can collapse the right part. Do you recognise the tram line there, and could you read the letters which appear below that tram line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you read that for our purpose so that we can hear the translation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I can mark it, if required. It reads "tram rails." It's by the figure 30. So between the arrow pointing north and the figure 30, it says "tram rails." And under that, it says "Telali Street." In the upper left corner, it says "Mosque." And the street going down is Oprkanj Street. By the spot marked "2," that is Oprkanj Street. And this matches the photograph, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Suljevic, it seems that this sketch is consistent with the photo on which you marked previously?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, although I'm not sure whether that wall was the wall of the shop or the wall of the building closest to the spot marked "2." But it's 100 per cent certain that this is the site. That's what we established.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that there is a mark for geographic north?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Where is this place, then? Where is the tram line in the north, in the part next to the town hall or elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the part of the tram line which goes toward Bascarsija from the town hall.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Let us see the shutter once more, and that's page -- I think it's page 40, this metal shutter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How do you explain that there are some markings on the shutter, most probably marked by chalk, whereas we see now no damages inflicted by fragments on the wall?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't dare claim that, based on this photograph. If we were to examine it more carefully, we may be able to find some damages, but they aren't marked. But the narrative under the photograph says that the purpose of this photograph was to show the damage done to the metal shutter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does that satisfy you, as an investigator?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, one may refer to it as to the scope of our authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now we'll speak about the photographs made by your investigators. I think that it's ERN 102-5429 -- ERN 102-5429? Yes, this is the photograph. Can you explain to us what this depicts?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This photograph shows the place of impact of one of the projectiles, and that's what the narrative under the photograph says. It says: "Place of where a projectile fell on the curb of Oprkanj Street," marked by figure 2."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Where do you see this number 2?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 2 is on the sketch, but I can maybe mark the crater, itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, please do. We can see the number 2 here.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How do you, as an expert, account for this semicircular arrangement of objects in the background, and the arrangement is convex toward the crater as if something had fallen there, rather than here?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand what it is that you're putting to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please connect these bits and pieces in the background on the white surface. Can you connect them with a line?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the fragments, these pieces?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, the pieces that you can see here. Can you draw a line that would all connect them?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One line to connect all the pieces? [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do continue.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How do you account for the semicircular arrangement of these fragments and the convex shape from the vantage point of the place of impact?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously, these are not fragments of projectiles, certainly not the larger pieces. I don't know what their origin is. And what is due to the first projectile and what is due to the explosion of the second one, I also can't tell.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did the investigation established that?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The investigation established that the spot marked "2" was the crater where one of the projectiles exploded, and the second location, which must be to the left somewhere, there is another crater where another projectile exploded.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did the investigation establish what these two black, most probably, metal parts are, where they came from, and what made them be arranged in this manner so that they are convex towards this side and concave to the other?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The purpose of the investigation that we conducted was to collect fragments of the projectile. We didn't collect any other fragments on site, and they weren't sent to us for analysis to establish their origin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What exploded here, Mr. Suljevic?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We should -- we would have to look at the report. Two artillery shells exploded here, which was established, and the calibre was 76 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you collect fragments here at this site?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And based on the fragments, an expert analysis was made and a report was produced.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, why do you think -- why did you think that it was of no interest to the investigation to establish the reason for this impossible arrangement of these fragments and two black pieces at the site? Why wasn't this registered and accounted for?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The purpose of the investigation was to establish the direction from which the projectile had come and to collect all traces of the projectile to establish its type, or the type of the two projectiles that were activated at this site.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Suljevic, I'm dissatisfied with your answer. The purpose of the investigation is to establish everything, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's not for the witness to answer those questions. Please go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: He's inviting speculation from the witness. The witness has explained as well as he can. Much of this is highly irrelevant, in our submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Agreed. I think -- I haven't counted the time, but I think you have less than half an hour. Please try to conclude your evidence as soon as possible, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is really deplorable, then. Then I cannot dwell on this any longer, and I must move on to Mis Irbina, which was admitted as a Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But, Mr. Suljevic, I must say to you that this is extremely sloppy and unusable for criminal law purposes. You don't know what happened, what the weather was like. You don't know what you established. When you came to the site, you had limited objectives of the investigation to accuse the Serbs for propaganda purposes. But in criminal proceedings, this is not good enough. You do not have relevant evidence that we can rely on to prove what happened on the flea market.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: You're making observations, which you are entitled to make in the Defence case, but there is no point in putting a series of statements to a witness. They are not questions. You are simply making observations, which is tantamount to giving evidence. As the President has indicated, you are wasting precious time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, I have stated some claims, and I'm asking the witness to confirm it or not, because I'm claiming that all these incidents in Sarajevo were staged, and I'm saying that the evidence do not allow me to conclude anything, or actually disqualifies this for the purpose of criminal proceedings. I want the witness to say what he has to say to this claim.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, the witness is not able to answer that question, since he was not there. And you can make that submission later on, as Judge Morrison indicated to you. Are you minded to tender the previous exhibited documents into evidence, i.e., the 65 ter 13172, the whole of it, or you're minded to only those parts which you used?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The parts which I used.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And I would kindly ask Mr. Suljevic to note the date and his initials on this page as well, and then I will tender it too.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If my memory's correct, Mr. Karadzic didn't use many pages, about five of them or six of them, and most of them were translated, I take it. But you would like to have the entire document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, parts of this dossier have already been admitted, not all of the parts which have been discussed with the witness. It might be just easiest to admit the entirety of 65 ter 13172.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can you give us an indication of the number, the exhibit number which we already admitted, albeit in a partial manner?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. Parts have been admitted as P1317, 1318, 1319, and 1320.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Well, then we'll admit it in its entirety, and we'll mark it for identification until we have a full translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. In respect of the translation, as I mentioned earlier -- in respect of the photographs, for example, the translations of maybe 15 or 20 pages are reproduced on 2 pages in the English, so I believe it is, in fact, a full translation, although the number of pages in English --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I take your word. Then we'll admit it. We'll give it a new Defence number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That will be Exhibit D554, and the photo will be Exhibit D555.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Let me just say, for the transcript, that we have not clarified the line for humanitarian aid in Dobrinja, not Alipasino Polje, nor Safeta Zajke.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Suljevic, can you help me, what was the previous name of the Safeta Zajke Street?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was Drinska.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And what about Safeta Hadzica Street, what was its previously name?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps Prvomajska, but I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Now I have to move on to Mis Irbina Street. Can you please consider that I be granted another session, or at least half of another session, because it would be a pity if this witness left without helping me clarify some issues. And until you decide, could we please have 14945, 65 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How long would you need for your re-examination, Mr. Gaynor?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Very little time at the present, not more than 10 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We've just decided that you will have another half an hour in the next session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the incident in Mis Irbina Street, number 18, which occurred on the 27th of June, 1995?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the report about the incident, what we can see on the screen right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So this is the report. Can you just briefly tell us what was established by the expert analysis in this case?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The request was to establish what sort and calibre of the projectile was and what was the direction from which it flew in. Could we please see page 2 so that we can see what the conclusions are or, rather, the opinion? And the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you just briefly explain to us what was established in the expert analysis?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was established that in this incident, a contact fuse shell of the 120-millimetre calibre for a mortar exploded. And on the basis of the azimuth, which was taken down, the direction from which it came was established.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What does it report say? Where was it launched?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The report says that the direction which was established on the scene corresponds to the enemy positions in Miljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Suljevic, when you say "Miljevic," then you also take a position in terms of the distance; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The report doesn't say that. It says that the direction corresponds with the direction of the enemy positions in the general Miljevici area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us try to say that again. Between Miljevici and the place of impact of the shell, are there any other positions?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the separation lines are there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, did you say this incident had been taken out from the indictment?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the incident, but this has been admitted. This has been admitted in evidence with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Gaynor, could you help us?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. The correct position was it was an unscheduled incident, so it never was in the indictment. We have included it in the amalgamated statement of Mr. Suljevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Should we call up the map of Sarajevo so you could show us where Miljevici are, where the place of impact is, and who was between these two places? Or, as you said, these were the separation lines. That means the Muslim position as well?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no doubt about that, because Miljevici were in an area controlled by the Army of Republika Srpska, and it's normal that between these positions and Sarajevo were the separation lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: With both Serbian and Muslim positions; correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, on one side was the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and on the other side was the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When you said "Miljevici," you didn't just mention the direction but also the distance, and why couldn't it have been launched from the separation line in the same direction?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the azimuth was measured, and simply in every incident, with every projectile which fell on the city of Sarajevo, one could say that it flew from the direction where enemy positions were located during the war, that is to say, the positions of the Army of Republika Srpska, because Sarajevo was surrounded on all sides throughout the war with the Army of Republika Srpska, and between the Army of Republika Srpska and the BH Army, there were, of course, separation lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So your position is that it was the Serbian position, though it could have been Muslim, and it could have flown from the same direction; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Serbian, it was certainly Serbian, just like all the other projectiles which were falling on the city of Sarajevo, including everything up to the modified aerial bombs.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we just please call up map number 1 from this special Sarajevo-specific court binder. And the number up there is 0546-6574. It's map number 1 from the special binder. The ERN number is 0361-5780. If that can help us, that's the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'm told that's P815.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Suljevic, may I kindly ask you to mark approximately where Mis Irbina Street is located. You can see where Skenderija is. So in relation to Skenderija, where is Mis Irbina Street?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could we please zoom in a little bit, because nothing can be seen here as it is, not even Titova Street, let alone Mis Irbina.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we then please zoom in on the part below which are the words "SA Centar," and then you see the Okur [phoen] area. If we can zoom in even more in the central part. Yes, that's what I mean, the densely-populated area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you see where Skenderija is close to the separation lines here; that is to say, next to the municipality border, and the separation lines were at the Jewish cemetery. Can you find your bearings on this map?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is approximately where [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's Skenderija, that's where Skenderija is. Could you please mark it with number 1?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And further on after Skenderija is Djuro Djakovic Street. Can you please find your bearings, approximately, and try to find Mis Irbina Street?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can just approximately say where it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That will be fine, thank you.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we now show the total image, and if you can then draw a line depicting the direction of Miljevici. Can you please mark this with number 2?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we will lose this if we now zoom out, then I would ask for this to be marked and admitted. Number 1 is Skenderija and number 2 is approximately Mis Irbina Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you now please just note the date and write your initials?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I move to tender this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D556, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see the whole image, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you now indicate approximately where Miljevici is located?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could we please see the report again, because I don't know the azimuth. I have to see where Miljevici is. I cannot see it unless we zoom in. So if I can just see what the azimuth was so I can determine what the direction of Miljevici is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You can have a look at the report. Do you have it with you? I will provide you with it. Number 14945, that's the report.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This had been admitted as Exhibit P1335, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Speaking for myself, Mr. Karadzic, I think this exercise is a waste of time, because the witness already confirmed there was a Muslim position between this place and Miljevici. So asking the witness, who is not an expert on geography, to mark on the map is a total waste of time. You have --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree Miljevici is somewhere around the place on the map where it says Novo Sarajevo? So that we shouldn't waste any more time, if we bring up the map again where it says "Lukavica" and "Novo Sarajevo," do you agree that it's there, and you have confirmed that the direction would cross the separation line up there on Trebevic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we then agree that children of your boss, Mirza Jamakovic, were also involved in this incident?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did one of these children lose its life?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, one was killed and the other one was injured.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did Mr. Jamakovic lose his hand on that occasion or did that happen earlier?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That happened earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How did he lose his hand?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, I was not a member of the MUP, so I do not know the details of the incident. But I think that a hand-grenade exploded in his hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: A hand-grenade or some other device?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, it was a hand-grenade.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see 1D02342.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I note the time. We'll have a break for half an hour. Before we do that, Mr. Robinson, last week you referred to D459, for which the translation has been complete, and you asked for admission of the document. We'll do that. So we checked the document, and the document is ready for proper admission. But in the future, for the convenience of the Chamber, I would like you to file a written submission, covering a number of MFI'd exhibits, instead of informing the Chamber the prepared exhibits in a piecemeal fashion. That would be much more convenient on the part of the Chamber. My understanding is that you e-mailed our Legal Officer a number of exhibits, so if you could file a motion in that regard as well. We'll resume at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Welcome, Ms. Edgerton. You will have half an hour, Mr. Karadzic, to conclude your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. With kind co-operation, Mr. Suljevic, we'll be able to achieve all that, I hope, although a great deal will remain unexamined. 1D0342, could we have that now in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise this report, Mr. Suljevic?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but we didn't compile this report. It was one of the members of the CSB who did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But here it says, number 6, that you took part in this too; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Since we haven't got much time, I would like to ask you to look at the one-but-last sentence: "At the moment of the fall ..."

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "At the moment of the fall, an explosion of the artillery projectile in the yard, as well as at the two entranceways, number 18 and 20 in the Street of Mis Irbina, children from the neighbouring village were playing."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So could you please explain this to the Trial Chamber? In the yard and also in the entranceways of these two particular street numbers; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what's written here.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please read this from the beginning? Actually, starting with: "Calibre 100 --"

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Calibre -- 122-millimetre calibre fell and exploded on the surface near Mis Irbina. The artillery projectile was fired from the positions of the aggressors, from the south-west, azimuth 205 degrees, which corresponds to the aggressor's positions on the locality of Vrace. When the projectile fell due to the explosion at the entrance number 18, Mis Irbina Street, the following person --"

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That will do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Suljevic, did you say 122 millimetres or 120 millimetres?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should have said "120 millimetres," that is what's written here. So a correction has to be made. It's 120 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And now it says here that someone was killed?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Jamakovic, Haris, son of Mirza, mother's name Azra, born in 1984, permanently residing in Mis Irbina number 18. Serious bodily injures were sustained by the following persons: Children who were playing in the yard at the moment when the explosion took place. 1. Jamakovic, Jazenka born in 1981, residing in Mis Irbina, number 18. "2. Habul Adi [phoen], born in 1981, residing in Mis Irbina, number 18. "Milan Trsic, residing in Mis Irbina, number 20. "4. Davor Mitic, born in 1979, Sutjeska number 2. "Alija Strogorac, born in 1962, residing in Mis Irbina, number 20," and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think the witness has to read all that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, he doesn't have to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: However, Sutjeska 2 is my address, and there was no Mitic family living there. Is that some kind of mistake?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you that I was not the person who compiled this report, and I was not present when these children were removed, were taken to hospital, those who were seriously wounded. I don't know the names.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Perhaps somebody moved in in the meantime. Just let's deal with one more sentence: "In the entrance ..."

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "At the entranceway of the building in Mis Irbina, number 18, where Haris Jamakovic was killed, large pools of blood were noted, as were remaining shrapnel that went through the metal door."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does it seem that in the yard and at numbers 18 and 20, Mis Irbina, children from the neighbouring buildings were playing?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Some children were in the yard, and others were in the building itself, the entranceway.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That's right. Somewhere in the stairwell too?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's inside. I don't know if it's the stairwell exactly. It's probably somewhere near the entrance, since they were injured.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have 1D2194. 1D2194. Can the previous document be admitted, unless it's been admitted already?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: No objection. I don't believe it's been admitted already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll mark it for identification, pending translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: MFI D557, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please mark the location where the projectile fell? Could you mark that on this map, please?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]. It should be around here or in that area, but that's where that entranceway should be. There's a passage from Mis Irbina, and I think this is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please write the date, and could you initial this?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, it will be Exhibit D558.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I would just like to note for the record, Mr. President, that this again is a post-conflict map, and the witness is marking --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We dealt with this map when we admitted D552, on which the witness marked the place where the -- I don't remember -- Schedule G14 took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Branislava Djurdjeva, to the north on this map. When did you arrive on the scene as regards this incident?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know how many times you've already asked this. I think the reports say when the on-site investigations started, because I saw a few moments that it says when it was over. We usually came there immediately after a particular incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please don't get angry at me, Mr. Suljevic. If you were testifying viva voce, that would be a very important element in terms of your credibility, but that's why I'm asking you. To the best of your recollection, when did you get there, what time of day was it? You compiled a report concerning your expert examination of the site of the explosion; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What we saw was your report; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How was it that you concluded that this had come from the aggressor positions?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It came from a direction that corresponds with the positions of the aggressor in the area, as stated in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Briefly, the same question: The aggressor positions, the Serb positions, that is, from there to the point of impact there's also a Muslim line, isn't there?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Any projectile that fell on Sarajevo, I mean, between the point of descent and the Serb positions, there were the separation lines as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your report, 024-233576, dated the 13th of July, you gave your opinion that this 120-millimetre shell that -- came from the Serb positions in the broader area of the area concerned. And you and your boss, Mirza Jamakovic, signed this report; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, but I have to confirm it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The ERN number is --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We did not catch it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's the second page, and that's where the signatures are. Can we have it on the screen, 02 -- 14945 is the 65 ter number. This map has already been admitted. P1335, it's been admitted as P1335. This is the first page. Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What is requested is to establish the calibre and the direction from which it came. Is the distance noted here from where it had been fired?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It says here that this is what was requested, expert analysis of the traces of explosion and the direction from which it had come.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Why does the previous document from the MUP say "from aggressor positions"?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says "from the area that corresponds with the positions of the aggressor." That's where the projectile came from.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jamakovic lives on this address. One of his children was killed and one of his children was injured. Is it customary for a victim to participate in an investigation?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, the victim did not take part in the investigation. It is correct that as chief of the department, he signed the report that I had worked on, but he did not take part in the analysis of the traces, themselves, and the analysis of the crater, either. I mean, I don't think anyone would have been capable of taking part in something like that in that situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the previous document, it doesn't say "in the direction." It says that it corresponds to the positions of the aggressor in the locality of Vrace. And in your report, it says "in Miljevici," so did you note this difference?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I stand by what it says in the report, that this direction matches the one stated in the report. From the direction of Vrace, it's all from that direction, and that -- and that coincides with those degrees.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now see P -- correction, 1D02343. 1D02343. I'm afraid that this is not usable. Can we see the following page, please. Yes, that's the one. The ERN number, or the last three digits, are 488.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you explain what this is about?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a yard where a projectile landed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What are these bags?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that this was the place where a police officer had his position, because behind his bag there is the CSB very nearby.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So what would you call this? This bunker made of sandbags actually protects the sentry of the CSB?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you say how high this bunker is? You can see there is a car next to it and a man standing.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, considering all these, we could say about two metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is a bunker of this kind a legitimate military target, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If there's a police officer in here, and uses it to protect himself from shelling, then, to my mind, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the CSB is not a legitimate military target, either; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. But I can say, for myself, that I would have been carrying around a bunker with me all the time so as not to be hit. But I cannot say whether or not a police facility was a legitimate military target.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that 15.000 police officers in Sarajevo took part in combat activities regularly; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if there were that many police officers in Sarajevo at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the Laste and other police units were included in regular combat activities?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, but I don't know whether their headquarters was here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, is it wise to erect bunkers and then let children play around them?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The place where the children were injured is not even 20 metres away from this. What do we do with the children; not let them leave their apartments?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please mark here where the place of impact was? This is a photograph taken by your investigation group. This is your investigative material; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. The projectile most probably fell here [marks], but I don't really remember where exactly it was. Most probably it was here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And on the lower photograph?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. There is no arrow marking it. We can see that the bags are damaged [marks]. Even in the upper photograph, we can see the same section [marks]. But I don't know where exactly the projectile fell. I suppose it was here, but given the time that has passed, I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, whatever you say. Just mark where it fell, mark it in this photograph, and sign and date it, please.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, from today's vantage point, I would say that it fell on the spot marked "1" [marks], but as I said, I can't remember exactly where each and every projectile fell, and the exact hour when I arrived at the site, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is the place where one projectile fell; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this specific instance, yes. Whether or not projectiles fell here earlier without consequences, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document into evidence, and I'll show a sketch. Maybe that will make things easier for you. Can we please see 1D2344, if this document is admitted. Maybe it's in the OTP's associated documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You're tendering only this page, the picture on which the witness has marked? Yes, it will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There will be more. I would like to tender the entire document, and I believe that the OTP tendered at least the statement of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think the previous report was admitted as Exhibit P1335, and we'll admit this marked photo as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D559.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see 1D2344. It's a sketch that may assist us -- or actually assist you to clarify things. The same document, page 2, actually. The ERN -- the last three digits of the ERN number are 487 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, 497, the last three digits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Last page of that document, 1D2344, page 3. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this the sketch of the event that happened in Mis Irbina Street, Mr. Suljevic?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you mark these elements in the sketch: the bunker, the CSB, the entrance to the building, and the place of the explosion?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, I believe that this is the location of the bunker [marks], and I can mark it "1" [marks]. This may not be very precise, but the entrance is here [marks]. That's the building number 18.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mark it "2," please.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]. And the CSB is hereabouts [marks]. I'm not sure how far it is, but it's the block of buildings that goes as far as the La Benevolencije Street that meets Mis Irbina Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Then mark it "3," please.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And number 2 marks the buildings numbers 18 and 20?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is actually building number 18. This building 20 could actually be here [marks], because there's another entrance there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could this structure of an unusual shape be the bunker?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't this size, because you saw in the photographs that it has a rectangular shape, a square shape.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, where did the shell land?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see no legend, so I can only suppose that the distances marked are the distances between the crater and some landmarks.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we perhaps reduce this and exhibit the legend, too, for the benefit of Mr. Suljevic? But if that cannot be done before saving the document, then we should first date and mark it and then save it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, you'll have five minutes. We'll admit this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D560, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That won't do, by any means, but what can I do? Can we please see the previous page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you will see, Mr. Suljevic, that the spot marked "1" by you is actually the place of impact. "1" stands for the place of impact or crater?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you see this structure that resembles a spade in shape has next to it the bunker marked "18." How do you explain that the fragments went through all this and hit the metal door at the entrance of building number 18?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what exactly your question is. But from the spot where the projectile landed, there were no obstacles in the direction of that entrance. And with regard to that spade-shaped structure, well, I don't know. But, anyway, from the place of impact to the entrance, there were no obstacles.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But if north is up, on which side did the shell actually fall; in the north, south, east, or west?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the legend, the projectile landed here [marks]. The square, to my mind, represents the bunker. And that other shape, I really don't know what it is. Maybe it's a lawn or something. But there was nothing between that structure made of bags and the entrance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What is the distance between the place of impact and the entrance to building 18?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we can tell from the sketch, but I think it may be up to 30 metres, if at all. But we don't have to speculate. We just have to enlarge the sketch.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says "17 metres 16 centimetres." Is that possible?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is, and I'm sure it's accurate.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D02343, please. The page is 490, the three last digits, that is, and it's the third page of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Shall we keep this new version of the witness's marking with blue?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I was just going to object to this procedure, in general, that the witness has been asked to make markings before he was provided with the legend to the map. The legend, itself, describes the locations on the diagram. What the witness is essentially being asked to do is carry out a memory test about an investigation that he participated in over 16 years ago, without having the opportunity to review the legend and the diagram beforehand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I was minded for him to read the legend, but given the time, I just let it go. But it's on the record, and we can bear that in mind when we are reading his evidence again in the future. Let's move on. But we'll admit this as a new exhibit, Exhibit D561.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I kindly request another 15 minutes just to finish at least this incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, you will have five minutes from now. You have to finish by 20 to 2.00. You have just exactly five minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It will be insufficient, you will see. Well, I won't be able to complete it. I'll break off. Could we see 1D02343. While we're waiting, let me just say that it's unfortunate that we don't have more viva voce witnesses, because then we would have problems in this courtroom. Let us see the following page of this document, 490.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this the door through which the fragment flew, and is that marked "3" on the door?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a door. And as we can see, number 3 marks the spot that was probably caused by the fragment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please mark it for us and explain to us what -- this one fragment, only one, that went through the metal door, what did it cause inside the building? It killed one child in there and wounded several; correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see that it says anywhere that one fragment killed one child and wounded several. If -- this reads that this was a damage probably caused by a fragment. I can see damages to the wall, but I don't want to go to speculation now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, please do not consume my five minutes. Tell me, did anything happen to those children behind this door? What happened on the ground floor and what happened on the first landing? You know what happened. You investigated it. Children were playing cards there, and somebody came to harm. How did those shrapnel enter?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could only come from -- could only have come from here [indicates]. Maybe the door wasn't fully closed. Don't make me speculate now. The children were in the staircase. Maybe they were standing next to the door. One boy was wounded outside. I don't know whether he was coming out or going in. But according to the statements, one boy was wounded outside, and the others in the staircase. Whether the door was closed, as in this photograph, or fully open, I really don't know. And let me not speculate, because this photograph was taken after those injured and killed had been taken away.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How does this door open? Does it open inward or outward?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Usually, such doors open on the yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But, sir, if you can't tell us who was hit here, who was injured or killed, if you cannot tell us, then who can? And what about the children behind this door?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You must take all the reports and the entire file and review it to learn all the details. What we did was only to establish the type of shell, its calibre, and the direction from which it had come. Other reports that are parts of the file, it probably can be found there, and you have to review that if you want to know all these details. Based on this one photograph, it's impossible to go into further analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Suljevic, you are here. We are fortunate enough to have you here. So can you explain to us how these children were the victims of a Serb mine, as you had put it, in an entranceway where the door was closed? The children were victims, but there were other children who were victims on the landing as well; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: All speculations. I will allow you two more questions, and that's it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With all due respect, Excellency, this is not speculation. There are statements that we're going to put to the Trial Chamber when we have enough time, and they are going to show all of this inconsistency involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, the last two questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Suljevic, I have no feeling whatsoever towards the evil tongues that say this: This could have happened because Mr. Jamakovic had some devices that were being prepared there in his house, some explosive device was being prepared there, and the Serbs have to be accused of that. What do you say to that? Is it very strange that this happened where Jamakovic lived and he is precisely in that line of work?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that what you are saying is totally exaggerated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Secondly, Mr. Suljevic: When you worked on all of these investigations, did you count on all of this reaching some court of law or was this done only for the purpose of blaming the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These reports were not done to blame the Serbs. They showed what it was that had been established on the scene. It is true that on-site investigations were carried out - how should I put this? - according to a faster rhythm due to the circumstances involved. If we were to carry out on-site investigations for two days, we wouldn't have enough time to carry out even a small part of the necessary on-site investigations. However, on the scene, we made an effort not to leave before the scene was properly viewed and before all the circumstances were clarified, those that were required by the judge who was in charge of the on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You did not answer my question. For what purpose was this done; for the purpose of being presented in a criminal court or for propaganda purposes?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did nothing for propaganda purposes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: He answered the question. Before I give the floor to Mr. Gaynor, two things. If there remains some part which you couldn't cover, it's purely because you didn't conduct your cross-examination efficiently. Secondly, you promised to ask -- that you will come back to the witness's prior statement you referred to. Do you have that reference now?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm still looking for it, Excellency. With your leave, we are going to put it when the next witnesses come from the same investigation team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: We have no questions in re-examination, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Then it concludes your evidence, Mr. Suljevic. Thank you for coming to The Hague twice, and now you are free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll have a protected witness for the next witness. There are a couple of rulings I'd like to give in relation to that witness, so for that purpose we'll go into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Now we are in public session, and, Mr. Gaynor, you may be excused.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The next witness is a protected witness. And to hear his evidence, we need to go into closed session. Before that, Mr. Robinson, do you have anything to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. President. We would like to make a motion to postpone the testimony of this next witness, pending appeal of the decision that the Trial Chamber rendered in private session. That held that the witness would not have his protective measures modified and that no inquiry would be made concerning the circumstances to the witness, and before continuing those protective measures. We believe that certification to appeal that decision should be granted, and I'm speaking simply now about the decision of whether to inquire with a witness, who has been completely unavailable to the accused or the Chamber, whether or not protective measures should continue for that witness, and, if so, what objective reasons exist at this time for continuing those protective measures. This is a witness who we requested meet with the accused prior to giving his testimony, and he declined, as is his right. And so the only information that the Chamber has is that given by the Prosecution, both in the earlier case, in which the Prosecution made those representations, and in private interviews with the Prosecution. And we think that it substantially and significantly affects the fairness of the trial that a witness can be given protective measures or protective measures can be continued without the opportunity of either the accused or the Chamber to determine for itself whether there are objective reasons for these protective measures to continue or even if the witness wants those protective measures to continue when asked in court by the Chamber, as opposed to by the Prosecutor. And I note the witness has been a suspect and has been notified of such by the Prosecution, which may influence his decision in that regard. We also think that an immediate decision by the Appeals Chamber on this issue is necessary, because it's going to be a recurring one. This is the first of several witnesses who will have protective measures concerning their testimony, and if the Chamber is not willing to provide an opportunity for such witnesses to be questioned about that in court, we feel that that could affect, ultimately, the outcome and fairness of the trial, and that it would be far better for the Appeals Chamber to have decided the issue at the outset rather than having recurring issues which may ultimately be found to be erroneous and under appeal from a final judgement. So for those reasons, we ask that you suspend the testimony of this witness, pending appeal, and that you grant us certification to appeal your decision today. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton or Mr. Tieger, do you like to respond to this submission?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I think our response should come as no surprise to the Chamber. We oppose the motion. The accused has essentially reiterated the arguments brought before the Chamber and rejected before. To some extent, I note that they -- the submissions slide over the fact that the Chamber made every effort, clearly, to ensure compliance with the Rules, and instead this is a continuing attempt by the Defence to somehow establish a new regime, after many, many years of an established practice, with respect to protective measures, a practice that has been followed by the Chamber in this case. So we oppose this and would note, in particular, that this witness's testimony has been scheduled for a long time, has been postponed already, as the Court will recall. We need to move forward, and there's no basis for again postponing this witness's testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will rise briefly, and we'll let you know whether we can continue or not during the course of today through the Legal Officer. --- Break taken at 2.02 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson, your motion for certification is denied. Written reasons will follow in due course. Let's bring in the witness. Before that, we go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 7th day of September, 2010, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.38 p.m.,
